cohort: The study included 303 female Multiple Sclerosis patients (aged >43 years) and 500 female controls (aged >45 years) who had reached the end of their reproductive period.
finding: Definitive childlessness was significantly more frequent in women with MS (22%) compared to controls (13%), with MS-related factors like disability, fear of transmission, and treatment concerns contributing to voluntary childlessness.
mod_finding: Multiple Sclerosis did not significantly affect the frequency of cesarean deliveries.
cross-section timing: Data was collected from participants who had reached the end of their reproductive period, retrospectively covering their reproductive lives.
